title: [internal] Gracefully handle peer closure during HTTP exchange creation
body:
**Requesting repo:** gsmlg-opt/ex_storage_service on branch `main`

**Severity:** nice-to-have

Gaoxy HTTP 0.12.0 logs a connection-process `MatchError` when an upload client cancels or closes immediately after submitting HTTP/1 request headers. Our storage transport intentionally tests short/failed upload sources and interrupted PUTs. The failed upload is rejected and no blob is published; the listener remains healthy and the complete normal transport suite passes. This request concerns graceful peer-close handling and avoiding an error crash log, not storage correctness.

**Dependency source:** `apps/ex_storage_service_cluster/mix.exs` uses Hex `gaoxy_http ~> 0.12.0`, whose declared source is https://github.com/gsmlg-dev/gaoxy.

**Reproduction:**

1. Start a `Gaoxy.HTTP` Plug listener on loopback with `protocols: [:http1]` and `http_limits: %{request_timeout: :infinity}`.
2. Send an HTTP/1 PUT with an explicit nonzero Content-Length, then close/cancel the client while request parsing is being dispatched (send no body or a short body).
3. Repeat to hit the peer-close race. The first socket identity lookup in `Gaoxy.HTTP.Exchange.new/7` can return `{:error, :enotconn}` and its success-only pattern match raises.

Our retained regression scenarios are `fixed-length upload rejects short and overlong sources without publishing content` and the interrupted PUT test in `apps/ex_storage_service_cluster/test/ex_storage_service_cluster/transport/http_test.exs`. The normal suite reproduced this multiple times with Elixir 1.18.5/OTP 28, `http_fetch 0.21.15`, and seed 20261022:

```sh
PAGER=cat ERL_FLAGS='+S 4:4 +SDcpu 2 +SDio 2' mix test apps/ex_storage_service_cluster/test --seed 20261022 --max-cases 1
```

Observed stack (request authentication headers omitted):

```text
** (MatchError) no match of right hand side value: {:error, :enotconn}
    (gaoxy_http 0.12.0) lib/gaoxy/http/exchange.ex:97: Gaoxy.HTTP.Exchange.new/7
    (gaoxy_http 0.12.0) lib/gaoxy/http/connection.ex:298: Gaoxy.HTTP.Connection.parse/2
    (hell 0.1.2) lib/hell/handler.ex:633: Hell.Handler.invoke_callback/2
    (gaoxy_http 0.12.0) lib/gaoxy/http/connection.ex:3: Gaoxy.HTTP.Connection.handle_info/2
```

The affected published source performs `{:ok, peer} = Socket.peername(socket)` and `{:ok, local} = Socket.sockname(socket)` without handling a closed socket.

**Expected behavior:** treat socket identity failure caused by peer closure as an ordinary closed/aborted connection, retain cleanup/admission guarantees, and keep the listener healthy without an exception crash report. No local dependency patch or handler workaround is being applied.
